description: Imperial / foreign stone-timber fringe — farmhouse shells, the Solitude dock family and keeled small craft. The foreign layer of the province: west/north-west fringe, Topal ports and road corridors only. Second sourcing pass adds the two Cyrodiilic flat-bottomed ferries and rowboat from Ships and Boats of Tamriel — the foreign river traffic of the Topal ports. TROPICALISED: `textureOverlayPools: ["tropical"]` puts Tropical Skyrim's retextures (vanilla filenames, architecture-TEXTURE-only — it ships no architecture meshes) ahead of the vanilla texture fallback, so the vanilla-backed pieces read hot and wet instead of Nordic grey. A pool's own textures still win, so the sourced-mod pieces keep their authored look. Drop the key to rebuild the un-overlaid variant. Woven wattle fence panels (fencewoven01/02 — Bethesda's most-placed fence, and the closest vanilla read to Argonian reed weaving) added 2026-09-04 so the marsh-repair fencing on the sheets is an actual wattle panel.

snapLogic.assemblies: Composites in this kit: `composite:farmhouse/farmhouse01-with-door` and `-farmhouse02-with-door` hang `farmhouseldoor01` at the offsets vanilla uses (templates vanilla:t0173 and t0335) — the rule that a farmhouse shell ships without its leaf. `composite:farmhouse/stonewall-run-3` and `-run-5` are the farmyard wall with its end pillars, on vanilla's own 7.27 m pillar spacing (group on stonewall01, 43 placements; templates vanilla:t0002, t0004, t0003) — the rule that `stonewallendl01`/`endr01` are caps and are never placed alone. The farmhouse wall and roof MODULES are not composited yet: they are a tileset, and a shell built from them is a building design, not a kit rule. Every single piece stays in the kit.

compose.note: The vanilla farmhouse shell with its door leaf. `farmhouse01` carries `farmhouseldoor01` at -1.82, -3.56, 0.0 m in the shell's own z-up frame, unrotated (template vanilla:t0173, 10 placements). The shell's own mesh has the opening but not the leaf, so a farmhouse placed bare reads as a hole in a wall.

The second farmhouse form with the same door piece at 0.0, -3.11, -0.01 m, unrotated (template vanilla:t0335, 7 placements). The mine also records a second, raised leaf at 3.18 m for the loft (vanilla:t0420, 6) — that is a loft hatch on a hayloft form and is left as a separate placement, since not every farmhouse02 has one.

The vanilla farmyard wall as its authors build it: a `stonewall01` span with an end pillar at each end — `stonewallendr01` at 3.64, 0.0, 0.0 and `stonewallendl01` at -3.63, 0.0, 0.01 m (group anchored on stonewall01, 43 placements; templates vanilla:t0002, 59, and vanilla:t0004, 54). Neither pillar is ever placed on its own: they are the caps that close a run.

Two spans of the same wall on one parcel: the pillar spacing is 7.27 m (template vanilla:t0003, 55 placements, measures `stonewallendl01` at -7.27 m from `stonewallendr01` — one span between two caps), so the second span sits at 7.27 m and its far cap at 10.91 m. About 14.5 m of yard wall in one placement, capped at both ends; longer runs repeat the module.
